#Canberra #Politics #Accountability 🌐

City Services Minister Tara Cheyne insisted that reopening the Big Splash 50-metre pool was a mandatory lease condition, not a mere aspiration.

The error confuses WHAT was publicly promised (a pool) with WHO is legally liable (Access Canberra and the leaseholder). Accountability vanishes behind semantic evasions.

The Big Splash saga is becoming as murky as the rainwater turning green in its abandoned pools.

Login or signup to continue reading

On Wednesday, it was another day, another Big Splash revelation.

This time, City Services Minister Tara Cheyne was in the hot seat.

In a Legislative Assembly inquiry, Ginninderra Liberal MLA Peter Cain brought up something Ms Cheyne had said on ABC News earlier this year, in which she was emphatic that the Big Splash owner had to reopen the 50-metre pool.

"It's not an aspiration. It's a condition. The pool must open," Ms Cheyne told the ABC on June 12, 2026.

At the time, Access Canberra had already announced that it would not revoke the Big Splash lease, partly due the leaseholder saying it would reopen the 50-metre pool to the public by November 1, 2026.

Access Canberra then changed its tune, announcing in September 2026 that as long as Big Splash opened an "unlicensed family restaurant" on the site by November 1, 2026, the leaseholder would be complying with the lease.

But at the time of Ms Cheyne's ABC interview in June 2026, the public was under the impression that the Big Splash leaseholder would be reopening the 50-metre pool by November 1.

Ms Cheyne's quote at the time confirmed that stance: "It's not an aspiration. It's a condition. The pool must open."

But when asked about it on Wednesday, Ms Cheyne was not as emphatic.

The minister said she would "own the quote" but believed she may have "misspoken" at the time.

"I'm prepared to say that I misspoke. I'm prepared to say that, but I need to check the record of that full interview. I don't have it in front of me," she said on Wednesday.

"I'm prepared to do so and come to the committee. I'm happy to apologise if I have misspoken. But I can't confirm that without the full record, and nor can you."

Ms Cheyne said she would check the context of the interview and report back to the committee.

Outside the committee, Mr Cain said that Ms Cheyne could not have been more clear in her quote to the ABC.

"This wasn't an off-the-cuff remark. The minister made a clear public assurance about what the government could enforce," he said.

"If that assurance was wrong, Canberrans deserve to know how it...
